problem: Find a vector equation of the line that passes through the points $M(0,1,0)$ and $N(3,4,-1).$
worked_solution:
The vector equation of the straight line passing through $M$ and parallel to $v$ is given by

$$
r=m+tv,
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty )$ and $m$ is the position vector of $M.$ 

We can find a direction vector by computing the displacement vector between the given points $M(0,1,0)$ and $N(3,4,-1)$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\overset{\to }{MN} \\  & =⟨3,4,-1⟩-⟨0,1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨3,3,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vector equation of the line is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
